eval_purpose: Verify the LIVE model behavior when the skill is activated: does it map capabilities intelligently (not auto-reject, not force-port), and does it produce a working Mistral package? Parser validation only proves format compliance — these evals prove (or disprove) the skill's actual intelligence.
how_to_run: Activate skill-porter in Vibe (Work: Context > Skills; CLI: skill in ~/.vibe/skills/), then send each prompt with the source package pasted/attached. Compare against the expected_behavior assertions. For a baseline comparison, send the same prompts in a fresh chat WITHOUT the skill active and diff the two outputs.

cases.prompt: I have a Claude Code skill for writing API changelogs. Folder: SKILL.md (frontmatter name 'changelog-writer', description with trigger phrases, body references Read and Bash tools, mentions running scripts/changelog_gen.py), scripts/changelog_gen.py (pure-python, reads a diff from stdin, prints markdown), references/style-guide.md (600 lines of writing rules), commands/changelog-full.md (a /changelog-full slash command with frontmatter name/description). I want it working in Vibe Work (chat.mistral.ai). Convert the whole package.
expected_behavior: Chooses the Vibe Work target without asking (user stated it)
Rewrites Read/Bash tool references into Work-appropriate phrasing (no read_file/bash left in the Work body)
Keeps the style guide as an attached file, does not inline 600 lines into the body
Makes a decision on changelog_gen.py per the decision tree (pure/deterministic → inline as steps OR attach; must state which and why)
Folds /changelog-full into the body as a workflow section, named so the user can trigger it by intent
Description rewritten as a 'Use when…' trigger, under 1024 chars
Delivers an import note: Title / Description / which files to attach
No [porter note] needed — nothing is unportable here

cases.prompt: Here's a Claude Code security skill. SKILL.md body says it installs a PreToolUse hook (hooks/security-guard.json) that blocks dangerous bash commands (rm -rf on project dirs, curl | sh), injects a checklist at SessionStart, and has a /security-audit command that fans out to two Task subagents (an attacker persona and a defender persona) and synthesizes their findings. It also has scripts/audit.py (walks local dirs) and references/threat-models.md. I want this in Mistral Vibe Code CLI.
expected_behavior: DOES NOT refuse the port merely because hooks/subagents are mentioned
Maps PreToolUse → Vibe hooks.toml pre_tool (with deny), and says the hook script needs adapting to the Vibe hook stdin/stdout JSON contract
Maps SessionStart injection → a body instruction (startup checklist), explicitly noting there is no session-start event in Vibe
Maps the two Task subagents → .vibe/agents/*.toml (agent_type subagent) spawned via task, noting single-hop/text-only limits
Maps /security-audit → its own user-invocable mini-skill OR a workflow section, with reasoning
Flags audit.py as CLI-only-capable (local dir walking) and keeps it for the CLI target with a runtime note
Reports an estimated surviving-usefulness percentage with a what-mapped-to-what list BEFORE or WITH the deliverable
Output contains a real hooks.toml and agents TOML that match the Vibe schema documented in references/

cases.prompt: This Claude skill is basically a plugin: its SKILL.md is 10 lines saying 'install the plugin to get marketplace skills', the real logic is .claude-plugin/plugin.json registering 15 marketplace commands, 4 hooks and 2 MCP servers that must run inside Claude Code's plugin runtime. There is no domain knowledge in any file. Port it to Vibe Work.
expected_behavior: Recognizes the core value is plugin-runtime plumbing, not skill logic — and says so plainly
Does NOT ship a full-looking Work skill with a dead centerpiece
Explains what the plugin did, why it cannot run on Work (no plugin runtime, no hooks, servers need deployment)
Offers the honest options: reduced port of any real content if it exists, or a clear 'not portable to Work'
No fake equivalence invented for the marketplace mechanism

cases.prompt: Port this OpenAI Codex skill to Vibe Code CLI. It's a normal SKILL.md (frontmatter name 'repo-summarizer', clean description) plus agents/openai.yaml with policy: allow_implicit_invocation: false, products: [codex-cli], plus references/structure.md and scripts/summarize.py.
expected_behavior: Identifies the source as Codex (openai.yaml present)
KEEPS agents/openai.yaml in the CLI output (Vibe reads it natively) instead of dropping or translating it
Checks the body for Claude-style tool names anyway (Codex skills sometimes reference them)
Notes the policy.allow_implicit_invocation: false maps to Vibe's disable-model-invocation
Delivers a flat ~/.vibe/skills/repo-summarizer/ layout with name matching the folder
